slides.heading: Creating Lists
slides.body: Creating Lists is part of Lists and Mutable Sequences. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Creating Lists
slides.body: Creating a list uses square brackets. Items are separated by commas and can be strings, numbers, booleans, or other values.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Creating a list is like writing several tasks on one checklist.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Lists use square brackets, zero-based indexes, and can be changed after creation.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create a list named numbers with 1, 2, and 3, then print it.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Create and print a list named colors with red, blue, and green.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
